content:
One of my favorite iPhone cases is back with a fresh new look. I used previous generations of the BitmoLab GAMEBABY case, and I fell in love the moment I started using it. It feels like an accessory designed specifically to tug at my nostalgic heartstrings. The biggest selling point of this case is that it isn't a separate accessory you have to carry around and remember to charge — it's a cleverly designed regular iPhone case that simultaneously doubles as a set of physical-button controllers, so you can play your favorite Game Boy ROMs (and other games). This is the perfect embodiment of "work smarter, not harder." No batteries or Bluetooth required, and setup is incredibly simple. If you're into any kind of retro gaming emulator, you definitely need to check this out.

Check out our hands-on video to see the case in action!

The design of this case is simple yet brilliantly clever. It uses a two-piece design, with the bottom half serving as the controller. When you're not gaming in everyday use, it functions just like a regular phone case. You get:

  • Tactile side buttons, including the lock button, volume buttons, and action button
  • Cutouts for the USB-C port, speakers, buttons, and camera control
  • Raised edges around the screen and camera module
  • Hard-shell plastic protection

But the magic is in the bottom half. That's where the gaming controls live — the buttons are well-made, feel solid, and are very satisfying to press. But how exactly does it work?

How It Works

As mentioned earlier, the smartest part of this design is that there are no electronic components inside, so no pairing process is required. The way it works is that each physical game button has a small capacitive contact point that mimics the effect of your finger touching the screen. It tricks the iPhone into thinking you're pressing on-screen controls, while it feels like you're pressing physical buttons. It's the same principle as the soft capacitive tips on those cheap touchscreen styluses.

A simple setup step is required to ensure the physical buttons are aligned with the on-screen controls. BitmoLabs provides all the necessary instructions via a QR code on the packaging. But it requires the Delta emulator app from the App Store. The app is completely free with no in-app purchases. Once you've downloaded the app, GAMEBABY offers a downloadable custom skin that places the emulator's virtual controls directly beneath the physical buttons. This skin is also free (you can download it even without the case).

Once you've installed the skin into the Delta emulator app, you're ready to play. You simply detach the bottom half of the case, flip it over, and reattach it to your iPhone. This way the controls align with the iPhone screen, giving you the feel of real physical buttons while playing retro games. When you're done gaming, slide the controller bottom out, flip it back, and snap it into place — and it's just a regular phone case again.

My Experience Using It

As I mentioned at the outset, I can't resist anything retro gaming — it triggers some kind of emotion in me and makes me want to replay the old Pokémon games from years ago. This product doesn't just make gaming more convenient; it provides a near-zero-friction experience. I don't have to remember to bring anything, don't need to charge it, and don't need to pair it. For me, remembering to bring extra accessories is always the biggest hurdle with any tech accessory, and this case eliminates that problem perfectly.

After using this case, I can feel that BitmoLabs has really stepped up the build quality significantly. The buttons have excellent tactile feedback — the moment you lift your finger, they spring right back up, and I never had any misinputs while gaming. I primarily used it to play all the classic Pokémon games, which are pretty casual titles that don't require super-fast reaction times. Even for games that demand quick reflexes, this case handles them well.

One trade-off to note: there's no MagSafe support. Because the case is split into two parts and the bottom half already houses the buttons, there's essentially no way to incorporate MagSafe functionality. So if you insist on having MagSafe in your phone case, this probably isn't for you. That said, if you have MagSafe accessories (I have plenty myself), it's easy enough to just remove the case to use them. It's also worth mentioning that this case doesn't have a cover for the camera control button — it doesn't make a huge difference, but it's still something to consider.

Pricing and Availability

GAMEBABY is available on the BitmoLab website and Amazon, starting at $24.99. There are three versions: GameBaby Color, GameBaby Retro, and the latest GameBaby Transparent (which is the one I've been showing). The GameBaby Transparent version is only compatible with the iPhone 17 Pro Max and is limited to a production run of 500 units, available exclusively on the BitmoLab website. The other versions work with iPhone 15 Pro and above, and are available on both Amazon and the official website. Another thing worth noting is that since there are no electronics, batteries, or Bluetooth, they can keep the price down to $25 — for a phone case, that's an absolute steal!

Wrap-Up

If you're like me and love revisiting retro games on your iPhone, this case is a no-brainer. It's inexpensive, lightweight, easy to set up, and genuinely enhances the experience of playing emulated retro games on the iPhone. Combine the physical buttons with the iPhone's excellent haptic engine, and it really does feel like playing a retro handheld console. With the current wave of nostalgic Pokémon game mods sweeping social media, this case with its haptic buttons is perfect for enjoying those games from the comfort of your home.

What do you think of this case? Would you consider getting one? Have you used one before? Let's discuss in the comments below!
